builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
summary: The Raw-injected Transformer replaces the standard v-prediction pixel-space flow-matching backbone with an architecture combining a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder and an output-side raw-input shortcut, separating semantic modeling from raw-state propagation so v-prediction becomes trainable without switching to x-prediction or a latent autoencoder. The cost is additional architectural complexity over a plain backbone, and it applies only when training a pixel-space diffusion model from scratch, which itself demands substantial compute. It can fail if the low-rank patch-PCA assumptions do not hold for a given dataset, and the ImageNet-scale evidence does not establish transfer to other resolutions, data distributions, or model sizes.
rationale: The finding is a training-methodology insight relevant only if the reader trains pixel-space diffusion models from scratch, which is infeasible under a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget, so it is worth tracking rather than adopting.
technique: Raw-injected Transformer for pixel-space flow matching

claims.statement: The Raw-injected Transformer replaces the standard v-prediction pixel-space flow-matching backbone with an architecture combining a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder and an output-side raw-input shortcut, separating semantic modeling from raw-state propagation so v-prediction becomes trainable without switching to x-prediction or a latent autoencoder. The cost is additional architectural complexity over a plain backbone, and it applies only when training a pixel-space diffusion model from scratch, which itself demands substantial compute. It can fail if the low-rank patch-PCA assumptions do not hold for a given dataset, and the ImageNet-scale evidence does not establish transfer to other resolutions, data distributions, or model sizes.
The paper reports that RiT restores effective v-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet 256x256, without a stated multiplicative improvement over a baseline.
